Companion Animal Travel Desk
Purpose: This section gives the team a simple way to handle animal travel check-in with steady, polite service.

The Companion Animal Travel Desk should greet every traveler in a warm, professional tone and keep the process calm for the pet and the person. Please review all details carefully, because small misses create avoidable trouble for both the traveler and the cabin team. <<FACT F086>> Staff should then continue with the rest of the check-in steps without delay or extra commentary. <<FACT F092>> If a traveler arrives with incomplete paperwork, the desk should explain the gap in plain language and ask for the needed item before the case moves forward. When an animal is accepted, the file should note the condition of the carrier, the comfort items, and any special handling reminders, since the cabin team monitors animals during flight and needs a clear handoff. For examples like Anika Silva with Ollie or Ravi Brown with a nervous cat, the same calm process applies, and the desk should avoid side comments that might sound sharp or rushed.

Water bowls, carrier checks, and other comfort items must be handled with care and treated as part of the safety routine, not as extras. The desk should not promise anything that has not been approved, and it should avoid guessing when the record is unclear. If the traveler asks for help, answer directly and kindly, then steer back to the required steps. When the check-in is complete, make sure the handoff note is easy to read so the cabin crew can support the animal properly in flight.

If anything feels uncertain, contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor at Aurelia Skyways for guidance.
